Hartnett sees a market still supported by aggressive dip-buying, but vulnerable to higher rates and tighter liquidity.

text: US AVIATION CHAOS: OVER 22,000 FLIGHTS CANCELED OR DELAYED America’s air travel system is struggling to recover from its worst nationwide flight shutdown since 9/11. A nearly five-hour FAA ground stop on Friday triggered roughly 10,000 cancellations and 7,000 delays. Another 3,700 flights were canceled and 2,000 delayed Saturday, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded. Officials traced the disruption to overloaded air traffic control systems, with critical radar and communications infrastructure affected. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is demanding $50 billion to modernize the aging system, calling the situation an emergency. Airline stocks are under pressure as the nationwide disruption continues.
